children.text: A green river flowing through lush palm forest in inland Bohol, famous for a river cruise where raft-style floating restaurants serve a buffet lunch with live music. Sitting on the road to the Chocolate Hills, it's a fixture on the lunch stop of any countryside tour.

The Loboc River rises in the Carmen highlands in the middle of Bohol, passes through the towns of Batuan, Sevilla and Loboc in turn, and empties into the sea off Loay in the south (the Bohol Sea); it is also called the Loay River. Its watershed covers about 520 km², and coconut and nipa palms, bamboo and tropical broadleaf trees crowd both banks. The water, which has passed through limestone country, takes on a deep emerald color on a clear day. It is about
24 km
from Tagbilaran, roughly
40 minutes
by car, and because it lies on the main road to the Chocolate Hills, it is almost never left out of a Bohol countryside tour.

What made the Loboc River famous is its floating restaurant cruise. A raft-style boat, with a roof and dining tables set on a twin-hull base, moves slowly upriver from the town pier while passengers eat a Filipino buffet lunch and listen to live singing. Partway along, the boat pulls up to a bamboo stage where village children and residents perform traditional dances and songs, and then it turns around in front of the small Busay Falls upstream and heads back down. The round trip takes about
1 hour
. Several operators run cruises, including Loboc Riverwatch, Rio Verde and Village Floating Restaurant, and prices are almost the same from one operator to the next.
Riverside Loboc is one of the starting points of the mission in Bohol. The Jesuits founded a mission station here in late
, it became a parish in
, and the present coral-stone San Pedro Apostol Church was completed in
. The ceiling paintings were done by Canuto Avila from
to
. The church lost its facade and part of its bell tower in the magnitude 7.2 Bohol earthquake of
October 15, 2013
, and it was restored under the supervision of the National Museum and reopened on
. The town is also home to the Loboc Children's Choir, which began as the Loboc Central Elementary School choir in
. The choir won top prizes at the national youth music competition (
and
), a gold medal at the Barcelona choir festival in
, and in
received the Gawad CCP Para sa Sining, the highest honor of the Cultural Center of the Philippines (CCP).

The cruise is quiet and takes almost no effort, so it suits trips with parents or children especially well. More active travelers can enjoy the same river in a completely different mood with a zipline across the gorge, early-morning stand-up paddleboarding, or a sunset firefly paddle tour. Be aware, though, that the cruise stops right away in rain or when a typhoon warning is issued, so leave some slack in your schedule.
Boats leave from the Loboc Tourism Complex pier for a round trip of about
1 hour
. Reviews say the Filipino buffet includes dishes such as fish sinigang, beef caldereta, pork barbecue, grilled fish, pancit and maja blanca, with drinks sold separately. Departures start around
and run roughly every 30 minutes, and the last boat leaves between

When the boat docks at the bamboo stage floating midway along the cruise, villagers and children perform traditional dances and play instruments, and sometimes invite guests to dance along. Tips for the performers are voluntary, and small bills of
are commonly used.

This is the small waterfall at the upstream point where most cruises turn around. It is not a tall, plunging fall but a low stream of water spilling along the width of the river, so keep your expectations modest and enjoy the view of the water blending with the forest. Many notices say swimming is not allowed here.

blocks.title: San Pedro Apostol Church and bell tower

children.text: It is about
from the tourism complex, a
3-minute
walk. The sights are the coral-stone facade with three arches and the four-story octagonal bell tower standing apart beside the church. Seven bells hang in the tower, and the oldest dates from
. On the third floor of the convent building attached to the church is the Loboc Museum, which displays church relics.
A zipline (about
) and a cable car span a gorge about
2.5 km
north of the town. Operations stop in heavy rain or typhoons, and prices change often, so check on site.
Riverside resorts such as Fox & The Firefly Cottages run stand-up paddleboard tours. The
2 to 2.5 hour
sunset course starts with a short lesson, then you paddle quietly in search of fireflies. The fireflies are wild, so some nights you won't see any.
This is a bamboo hanging bridge in Sipatan, Sevilla, about
10-15 minutes
by car from the town. The two parallel spans are each about
long and take only
2-3 minutes
to cross. Wet bamboo is slippery, so wear sneakers.

blocks.title: Combine it with a countryside tour

children.text: Loboc is the lunch stop on the central Bohol tour. See the
Chocolate Hills
and the
Tarsier Sanctuary
in the morning, then stop at the
Bilar Man-Made Forest
after the lunch cruise to complete a full-day itinerary.

Direct flights from Manila to Bohol-Panglao International Airport (TAG) take about
1 hour 20 minutes to 1 hour 40 minutes
and are operated by Cebu Pacific, Philippine Airlines and AirAsia. From the airport to Loboc is about
, roughly
50 minutes to 1 hour 15 minutes
by taxi, and the fare is about
. Many notices say Grab is hard to get in Bohol, so it is safer to book a car before you arrive.
From Cebu Pier 1 to Tagbilaran Port, the OceanJet, SuperCat and Weesam Express fast ferries take about
2 hours
. OceanJet runs up to around 10 trips a day, while Weesam has fewer. Economy costs about
and business about
, and the port fee is paid in cash on site. From Tagbilaran Port, take a taxi or tricycle to the Dao Integrated Bus Terminal and transfer to a bus.
At the Dao Integrated Bus Terminal in Tagbilaran, take a bus or jeepney bound for Carmen and get off at Loboc. The ride takes about
1 hour
and the fare is about
, depending on whether it is air-conditioned. Some buses will drop you in front of the Loboc Tourism Complex. From the airport, transferring by public transport takes
1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours 30 minutes
The most common way is to charter a vehicle for a countryside tour. A full-day charter from Panglao costs about

per vehicle, depending on the vehicle type, the number of people, and whether the driver acts as a guide. You can see the Chocolate Hills and the Tarsier Sanctuary in the same day, and tour packages often include the cruise lunch, so confirm this when you book.

The town pier and the church are within walking distance. For farther places such as the Sipatan hanging bridge and the Ecotourism Adventure Park, take a habal-habal (motorcycle taxi) or a tricycle, and negotiate the fare before you get on. Some operators also depart from the pier near the Loay bridge downstream, so check the departure point when you book.
The dry months of
December-May

are when the river runs clearest and the skies open up, so the green of the forest contrasts sharply with the color of the water. Midday is hot and humid, but the cruise boat has a roof and the river breeze makes it bearable.
During the
June-November
rainy season, soil washes down from upstream and the river often turns brown, and the cruise stops if the rain continues. In early January
, Tropical Storm Agaton (Urduja) flooded the town and operations were canceled, and the cruise, which was suspended after Typhoon Odette damaged the boats, resumed only on
March 1, 2022
. On
February 6, 2026
, the Loboc tourism office also halted all water activities on the river because of Tropical Depression Basyang, a precaution taken while the storm was still
650 km
away. Even in the dry season, the weather can stop operations suddenly like this, so check the latest announcements before you visit.
Around Holy Week, New Year's and long holidays, tour groups crowd in and the wait is said to grow from
30 minutes
to as long as
2 hours
. Checking in before
or going after
is much more relaxed. Fireflies are easier to see on nights with a weak moon, and one notice says sightings are reliable in the dry season (November-May), though they are never guaranteed.

children.text: Prices are rough estimates as of
and may vary with local conditions.
Most people visit the Loboc River as a day trip, but there are a few bamboo and timber lodgings along the river. Nuts Huts in Gotozon village costs around

a night, but reviews mention about 200 steps and no Wi-Fi or hot water. Fox & The Firefly Cottages has 11 traditional-style riverside cottages and runs its own paddleboard tours, and Loboc River Resort in Kamayaan costs around
a night with breakfast. Prices change by date, so expect a range of roughly
a night; if you want more amenities, stay on Panglao Island or in Tagbilaran city and visit as a day trip.

The cruise buffet is Filipino home cooking built around rice, grilled dishes, beef caldereta, sinigang, pancit, tropical fruit, and desserts such as maja blanca. Reviews say the food is decent and varied, so think of it as a meal to enjoy for the atmosphere rather than the flavor. Shops in town sell Bohol specialty snacks such as calamay (sticky rice sweet in a coconut shell) and kisses, a peanut candy, and buko juice (fresh coconut juice) from roadside stalls is a treat too.

Check in for the cruise at the information desk of the Loboc Tourism Complex. You are assigned a table and a boat and wait to be called, so arrive 30 minutes before departure. The desk will keep your bags next to the counter for about
each.
Cash is the norm. Prepare small bills in Tagbilaran or Panglao for tips, drinks and the hanging bridge fee.
Several boats run almost the same route, so sit at the riverside railing to get a proper view. The earlier you board, the better.
The line at the buffet gets long right after departure, so enjoy the scenery for the first
10 minutes
and then fetch your food at a relaxed pace. Drinks are paid for each time you order.
In peak season, it is best to book the day before by phone or Facebook message. For tour packages, check whether the cruise is included.
Paddleboard and firefly tours have limited group sizes and need to be booked at least a day ahead. Bring a waterproof bag, a change of clothes and mosquito repellent.
Good photo spots are the town bridge, where you can frame the river and church together, the front of Busay Falls, and the riverside bamboo performance stage.
Ride the zipline and visit the church in the morning, and take the cruise after 2 PM to avoid the crowded midday hours; splitting your schedule this way shortens the wait.
The fare rose from
to
in
April 2024
, and some notices report a further increase (
) since then, so confirm that day's price and any discounts you qualify for at check-in. Life jackets are provided on board, so be sure children wear one.

When the river rises or a typhoon or tropical depression warning is issued, cruises and paddle tours stop, even a day ahead. After heavy rain the current is strong, so do not swim or paddleboard in the river then, and follow the operator's instructions.
Do not lean on the cruise boat's railing or stand at the edge of the boat to take photos. The boat rocks when it turns.
Throwing trash or food into the river is prohibited. Many notices also say swimming in front of Busay Falls is not allowed.
Fireflies are easier to see in darkness and quiet. Do not shine flashlights or flash at them, do not make noise, and do not catch them.
Inside the church, covering your shoulders and knees is polite, and refrain from sightseeing photography during Mass.
Photographers on the boat or at the pier sometimes charge
or more later for photos they took. If you don't want them, politely decline from the start, and if you do plan to buy, confirm the price first.
